parameters.content:
## Gmail-Only Customer Channel (compulsory constraint)

Every customer-originated input in this workflow is read from Gmail — never a generic webhook. Webhook nodes are kept ONLY for system-to-system events with no human customer on the other end (Python fraud-score POST, internal ops-decision submission).

**Gmail Trigger nodes (customer replies parsed from email body):**
- Co-Signature Response → APPROVE/DECLINE for both-signature transfers
- Holder Vote Received → approve/reject vote on holder removal
- Holder Dispute Input Received → each holder's dispute input text
- Acknowledgement Received → CONFIRM / I ACKNOWLEDGE for add-holder-with-debt
- Fraud Self-Attestation Reply → customer's false-positive claim (queues ops review, never auto-releases)

See TRD §3 "Gmail-Only Customer Channel — Enforcement Detail" for the full writeup.

nodes.name: Manual Trigger: Seed Policy Index (Run Once)

parameters.content:
## One-Time Setup: Seed the Pinecone Index

This mini-branch is NOT part of the live 8 branches (A–H) — it is a one-time manual step to populate Pinecone before Branch D's RAG support can retrieve anything.

**Run this once, manually, before demoing Branch D:**
1. Click "Execute Workflow" on the Manual Trigger below (or open this node and hit the play button).
2. It seeds 8 placeholder bank policies (POL-001 to POL-008) into the `bank-policy-fraud-index`.

These policies are generated for this project since no real bank policy documents existed. If you later have real policy docs, swap the Code node for a document source (Google Drive, Postgres, etc.) and keep the Doc Loader → Embeddings → Pinecone insert chain the same.

Without running this once, Branch D will always return NO_CONFIDENT_ANSWER because the index is empty.
